**A note on the evidence.** Stereotype threat is firmly part of the tested curriculum and you should answer questions on it as described above. Be aware, however, that the size of the effect is contested. A meta-analysis of 47 effect sizes in schoolgirls found a mean effect of about 0.22 but several indications of **publication bias**, and the same group's later large-scale registered replication found no evidence of the effect in Dutch schoolchildren. The mechanism is well specified and the laboratory demonstrations are real; what remains unsettled is how large and how general the effect is outside the laboratory.

preserving the broader stereotype. Closely related is **expectancy violation**: because the stereotype sets up an expectation, a counter-stereotypic performance is registered as *surprising* rather than as disconfirming evidence. Observers react to the surprise — and then subtype the individual — instead of revising the category, which is why one impressive exception so rarely changes anything.

sources.title: Flore & Wicherts, “Does stereotype threat influence performance of girls in stereotyped domains? A meta-analysis”, Journal of School Psychology (2015) — mean effect 0.22 with several signs of publication bias
